b.x: A painting app for Windows, made for the way you draw: a pen on glass, two fingers for the canvas, and brushes that behave like your oil pastel and your curves. It runs on its own, offline, with no account. Your works are saved in Documents, in a folder called PL Paint.
Draw first. Everything else on this page is here for when you want it.
Nothing you draw leaves this computer.
The screen is four things: a thin strip along the top, one slim sidebar, cards that drop down from their buttons, and the canvas. Everything else gets out of the way.

x: Gallery
The list of everything you have drawn. Open a work, start a new one, or look at your Daily Mark.
Actions
The wrench. Files, the video of your drawing, guides, drawing assists and the settings.
Adjustments
The wand. Colour and picture effects such as Hue, Blur and Curves, applied to the layer you are on.
Selection
The S shape. Marks off part of the picture, so only that part changes.
Transform
The arrow. Lifts the layer so you can move, scale, rotate or bend it.
The name of the work
The title of the picture. Tap it to rename; it is the name shown in the Gallery.
Paint
The brush. Draws with the brush you have chosen.
Smudge
The finger. Pushes the colour that is already there, instead of adding new colour.
Erase
The eraser. Takes ink away. It remembers its own brush and size.
Layers
The stack of sheets your picture is made of. Open it to add, hide, reorder and blend layers.
Colour
The coloured circle. A tap opens the colour card; the circle always shows the colour you are painting with.
Size
The tall slider on the left. Makes the brush bigger or smaller.
Modify
The small square between the two sliders. Hold it and tap the canvas to pick a colour (the eyedropper).
Opacity
The slider below the Modify square. How see-through the brush is: low is faint, high is solid.
Adjust strokes
Opens the card that changes how strokes were drawn, after the fact: the last stroke, or every stroke on the layer.
Undo
Takes back the last thing you did. A two-finger tap does the same.
Redo
Brings back what you just undid. A three-finger tap does the same.

b.x: Left of the top strip are the tools for the whole picture: Gallery, Actions, Adjustments, Selection and Transform. The name of the work sits in the middle (double-click it to rename). On the right are the tools for marks: Paint, Smudge, Erase, Layers and the Colour circle.
The sidebar holds the size slider, the Modify square, the opacity slider, Adjust strokes, Undo and Redo. In Actions you can move it to the right-hand side.
Tap the tool you already have selected and its brush list opens.
Each tool, Paint, Smudge and Erase, remembers its own size and opacity.
The pen draws. Fingers move the canvas. A resting palm does not draw: while the pen is near the glass, touches are ignored.
How to

x: Draw with the pen. Pressure changes the width, and the lean of the pen changes some brushes.
Press the pen’s eraser end, if it has one, to erase.
Hold the pen’s side button to pick a colour from the canvas (you can give it another job in Gesture controls).
A pen with two buttons: press the second one to switch between the brush and the eraser, and press again to switch back (that button can run any action too, in Gesture controls).
No pen? A mouse draws, and Alt or the Modify square picks colour. Turn on Finger paints in Actions if you want a finger to draw too.

b.x: The strokes you draw keep the real path of the pen, so you can adjust them later.
Two fingers do most of it. Every one of these can be changed in Gesture controls.

b.x: Choose what each gesture does. Any action from the QuickMenu list can go on any gesture.

x: Each gesture, and what it does
One row for each gesture. Choose which action it does.
How long to hold
How long to keep two or three fingers down before the repeating gesture starts.
Back to the defaults
Puts every gesture back to how it came.

b.x: How to

x: Open Actions, then Gesture controls.
Pick an action for each gesture, or None.
Hold two or three fingers keeps repeating Undo or Redo; for any other action it runs once.
Back to the defaults puts everything as it started.

b.x: The pen’s side button can run any action too. The eyedropper is the one that works while held.
The second pen button runs its action on each press; out of the box it swaps the brush and the eraser.
Six buttons around a hexagon, where your pen is. Right-click, or press Q.

x: Six buttons, one profile
Your QuickMenu: six actions on one ring, saved as a profile you can swap.

b.x: How to

x: Open Actions and find QuickMenu to choose what each of the six buttons does.
Make a new profile (a copy of this one) when you want a different set for a different kind of drawing.
Tap the middle of the hexagon to switch profile.

b.x: There are more than forty actions to choose from: every tool in this handbook is in the list.
Pick a size, or type your own, up to about sixteen million pixels. Choose a paper, and switch on Transparent if you want no background at all.

x: Sizes
Ready-made canvas sizes: cards, a sketchbook page, a seamless tile, strips and more.
Your own size
Type any width and height in pixels, up to 8192.
Paper
The surface the picture sits on: plain, or a textured stock with a torn edge.
Transparent
Leaves the background out, so the picture exports with nothing behind it.
Create
Makes the canvas with the choices above.

b.x: How to

x: Open Actions, then New canvas (or the Gallery, then + New canvas).
Tap a size, or type a width and a height.
Choose a paper (see Paper, below).
Tap Create. The picture you were on stays in the Gallery.

b.x: The sizes include the card sizes of your physical work: ATC 2.5 x 3.5 in, small card 4 x 6 in, square card 5 x 5 in, a sketchbook page, a seamless tile and a long strip for cuffs and belts.
The ground can be plain, cream, deckled, canvas or black. Deckled paper has the torn, handmade edge of your oil-pastel studies, and the paper has a fibre you can see under the marks.
How to

x: Open Actions and choose a Paper, or choose it when you make a new canvas.
Other ground swaps cream for black and back, under the same marks. The channels, being clear, show the new ground.
A deckled sheet saves as a PNG with a transparent edge.

b.x: Transparent background is a switch in New canvas, in Actions and in the Layers card. PNG and SVG keep the transparency.
Every work you have drawn is kept here, with a picture, a size and a date.

x: Daily Mark: the days you drew, and the streak
A square for every day you drew, and the count of days in a row.
New canvas
Starts a new picture from the Gallery.
A stack of works
Several works kept together under one name. Tap it to open the stack.
A work
One picture, with its name and size. Tap to open it; press and hold for Rename, Duplicate, Stack or Delete.
Close
Closes the Gallery and takes you back to the canvas.

b.x: How to

x: Tap a work to open it.
On a work: Rename, Duplicate, Stack (put it in a stack with a name), Delete (tap twice).
A stack shows as one card. Tap it to open it and see its works; tap the arrow card to come back.
At the top is Daily Mark: a square for each day you drew, and the streak of days in a row.

b.x: Daily Mark counts strokes, not minutes. A day with one stroke counts.

secs.title: Saving, and getting your work back

b.x: The app saves by itself, three seconds after you stop, and never later than twelve seconds into continuous drawing. Every stroke you finish is also kept in a journal, so if the app is killed mid-drawing, only the stroke still in your hand is lost, and the rest comes back when you open it again.
How to

x: Save PNG (Ctrl S) saves the picture, with transparency if the background is off.
Save PSD keeps every layer: names, order, opacity, blend mode, visibility, masks and groups (as real folders).
Open PSD adds a PSD’s layers to the picture.
Save SVG, two ways: layers as embedded pictures, or the brush strokes as true vectors (width follows pressure). Fills, filters and pasted pictures are not in the vector one.
Open as layer brings any picture in as a new layer.

b.x: Everything is written to Documents, in PL Paint, so your own backup already covers it.
The wrench at the top. Files, the video of your drawing, the guides, and the settings that are not tools.

x: New canvas
Starts a blank picture. You choose its size and its paper.
Lift
Turns a photo of an ink drawing into a transparent layer of ink, with the paper taken out.
Study
Records how you draw (the real path, pressure, tilt, pauses) so a hand model can learn it. It stays on this computer.
Gesture controls
Chooses what each finger or pen gesture does.
Guides
Puts a grid, isometric lines or perspective lines on the canvas, and can snap your strokes to them.
Symmetry
Mirrors your strokes: down the middle, across, in four quarters or round a centre.
Tile
A mark that runs off one edge comes back on the opposite edge, so what you draw repeats with no seam.
Timelapse
Records the picture being made. Replay it, scrub through it, or save it as a video.

b.x: On a phone Actions is in tabs, in the order Procreate Pocket uses: Add (open an image or a PSD, copy and paste, from a photo), Canvas (new canvas, fit to screen, light and ground), Assist (Drawing Assist, Node mode, Echo Fill, Study), Share (save PNG, PSD, SVG, Sync, Send to Curate), Video (Timelapse), Prefs and Help. The tab bar scrolls sideways when it is wider than the phone. Stabilisation is a slider in Prefs: it steadies the line for every brush at once (0 to 100%), and a brush that has its own StreamLine or Stabilization keeps whichever is stronger. On the laptop it stays one list.

Actions holds: New canvas, the Save and Open buttons, the Timelapse buttons, Study, Gesture controls, the QuickMenu editor, Guides, Symmetry, Tile, Tangent Lock, Facet and Curve, Passes, Light and ground, Lift, Name it, Paper, Copy and paste, Echo Fill, and Prefs (right-hand sidebar, finger paints, the debug overlay).
Brushes are kept in packs. Tap Paint, Smudge or Erase when it is already selected and the list opens.

x: Brushes
The brush packs. Tap a brush to paint with it; tap it again to open its settings.
Paint with each brush’s own colours
On: a brush uses the colours stored in it. Off: every brush uses the colour you picked.
Export this pack
Saves the pack as a file you can keep or share.
Import a pack or.abr
Brings in a pack of brushes, or Photoshop.abr brush files.

b.x: How to

x: Tap a brush to use it. Tap the selected brush again to open the Brush Studio.

The pack Basics is the plain set. His hand is the brushes that behave like your oil pastel and your curve hero. Glyph stamps are your glyphs. Mine holds brushes you make. Imported Photoshop brushes get a pack of their own.
Switch on Paint with each brush’s own colours and every brush in His hand paints in its own colour, so you can tell them apart. Switch it off to use your colour.

b.x: Export this pack saves a pack as a file you can keep or send. Import brings one back, with the same checks.
Twenty brushes, each made from a mark of yours and named for it. Every one cuts a clearance around itself, the way the curve hero does, and each has its own colour.

x: Oil pastel, Pastel wash
Thick wax with a bled, rough edge; the same laid light so the paper shows
Ledger pen
Thin, even, a little shake, no point
Curve hero, Curve pair, Curve
Flat-ended bands that swell and thin, and cut their own gap
Tube
A glossy double tube, light on one side
Crayon pair, Wax relief, Pastel bleed
A thick band with a thinner line beside it, or two parallel lines
Flat paint
Flat acrylic bands, a little dry-brush rag
Keyline hero, Glow curve, Stacked hero
The Channel filled in: a keyline, a glow, two stacked
Tooth pastel, Resolve ribbon, Support hero, Satellite pastel
Pressure that fills the paper, ends that fold closed or widen, marks dropped near the line
Weave hero, Echo pen
Over and under at each crossing; a band that draws its own echoes

b.x: Each brush’s settings are in the Studio. Change them, and the change is yours.
Tap the selected brush again. On the left, the sections; in the middle, the settings; on the right, a pad that draws with the real engine, so you see every change as you make it.

x: Sections
The groups of settings: shape, spacing, wobble, colour, lines and more. Pick one to see its sliders.
Settings
The sliders and choices for the section you picked.
Try it here
A pad to scribble on. It shows the brush as you change it, and nothing here goes into your picture.
Name
The brush’s name. Tap it to rename the brush.
Duplicate
Makes a copy, so you can change one and keep the other.
Reset
Puts the brush back to how it first came.
Done
Closes the studio and keeps your changes.

b.x: How to

x: Pick a section on the left.
Move a setting. The pad redraws.
Draw on the pad to try it.
Duplicate makes your own copy, Reset puts it back as it was made, Done closes.
Colours
The main colour and the accent colour, chosen from your house colours
Stroke path
Spacing, jitter, fall off
Stabilization
StreamLine and Stabilization: how much the line lags and smooths
Taper
How the start and the end thin
Shape
Round, square, diamond, bristle, tube or an imported tip; hardness, roundness, angle, scatter
Grain
Paper, noise, canvas, dots, relief; fixed to the paper, moving with the stamp, or along the stroke
Rendering
Flow, and which side the tube light is on
Companion line
A second line in the accent colour beside, or over, the main one
Parallel lines
One to three lines moving together
Clearance
The Channel, below
Wet mix
Picks up the colour under it
Hand
Tremor, slow swell, support base, how ends resolve, satellites, echoes, weave
Paper behaviour
Tooth, burnish, grain along the stroke, wick
Dynamics
Speed to size
Pen
Pressure to size and opacity, its curve, tilt to size and angle
Colour dynamics
Each dab a little different in hue, saturation and lightness

b.x: In your own rules, the clearance and the keyline are one object: a uniform gap that nothing crosses. Only what fills it changes. PL Paint gives every hand brush that gap, and lets you decide what is in it.

x: Clearance, its fill, a second channel
The gap left round each line, what fills that gap, and an optional second gap outside it.
The pad shows it as you change it
The sample stroke redraws as you move a slider, so you can see what each setting does.

b.x: How to

x: Open the Studio and go to Clearance.
Set the size of the gap. Clears at chooses the sides only (flat ends stay open) or all round (the head and tail too, for the thick single-line brushes).
Fills with chooses what is in the gap: clear (the ground shows through), a colour (a keyline), a glow, or a soft shadow.
Heavier side makes the gap bigger on one side of the line.
Second channel adds a second ring outside the first, with its own fill: light then dark, as in your plates.

b.x: A clear gap on a black ground reads as black; on cream as cream. Other ground swaps them without redrawing.

Six brushes for bands the way you draw them on cards: a filled middle with a thin line down each edge (sage with teal, salmon with purple, gold with obsidian, red with black), and Bone band, two bold black lines with a bone middle. The size is the whole band. Made from the photos of your cards (references 13 to 22 in the toolkit).
How to

x: Pick a band brush from the His bands pack. Its middle and its lines are two colours, chosen from your house colours; change them in the Colour card (the swatches: Main is the line, Middle is the fill).
One band over another: the band drawn last stays whole, with its edge lines across the other one, and the band under it stops at its outline. There is no gap, because the fill hides what is beneath.

One band growing out of another: start a stroke inside a band and it grows out of it. The brush reads the angle: leaving steeply it is a T (the first band’s outline stays whole), leaving along the band the outlines flow together.
One band ending in another: finish a stroke inside a band and it joins it: it stops at that band’s outline, and its own lines stop there too.

Round the corners (Band mode: round the corners) lets the band ease into a turn, so the edge lines sweep round a corner as one soft line instead of folding at a point. Swell the line thickens the edge line where it turns, the way a pen line does. The His bands brushes come with both on; turn them to 0 for the old sharp corner.

In the Studio, Parallel lines, Band mode sets how thick the edge lines are, The middle turns the fill on and Middle colour chooses it. The join is automatic: the brush decides from where you start and where you end.

b.x: The bands have no clearance gap, unlike the His hand brushes: the outline is what separates one band from another.
Bone band has a rough, crayon edge. The others are clean.
Top to bottom: the curve hero (a clear gap), the keyline, the glow, and two stacked channels.
These are the rules of your line language, as settings.

x: Tremor, swell, support base, resolve, satellites
Traits of your hand: a slight shake, a width that swells and thins, a base the line rests on, a line that resolves into another, and small marks that follow it.
Tremor
The hand’s shake. Each edge of the band shakes on its own, so the width wobbles too. Your spec puts it at 0.06 of the width.
Slow swell
The width rises and falls along the stroke even with no pressure, so a mouse can draw like a pen.
Support base
An end with no room to thin gets wider instead.
Resolve
An end can fold closed into a diamond or a teardrop instead of a flat cut.
Satellites
One to four small marks dropped near the line, the same place every time for the same stroke.
Echo pen
When you lift, the band draws its own inner echoes, concentric clear lines collapsing to the middle.
Weave
Where the stroke crosses an earlier one it goes over at the first crossing, under at the next, over at the next.

b.x: Four settings make the paper matter, the way it does with real oil pastel.

x: Tooth
Press harder and the wax fills the paper’s grain; press lightly and the paper shows through.
Burnish
Each stroke lays its grain in a different place, so a second pass fills what the first left.
Grain along
The texture is pulled out along the stroke, so it reads as streaks.
Wick
After a marker stroke the edge spreads into the paper, more where the paper is rough.

b.x: The paint on the brush picks up the colour of the layer under it, and slowly goes back to its own colour.
How to

x: Choose Wet gouache or Oil smear, or turn up Pick up on any brush.
How long it carries says how long it keeps the colour it picked up: at the top it never lets go.

b.x: Wet mix reads the layer you are drawing on, not the others.

secs.title: Brushes from files and from marks

b.x: Bring in Photoshop brushes, or turn your own mark into one.
How to

x: Import a pack or.abr (in the brush list) takes a Photoshop brush file. PL Paint reads its tips, names and spacing. Photoshop’s dynamics, scatter and texture are not carried over. The first 120 tips of a file are taken.

Make a brush (in the Layers card) turns the marks on a layer into a stamp brush in the pack Mine. Draw your signature on a layer, tap it, and it is a brush: a tap stamps it, Size makes it bigger, and it paints in whatever colour you have.
The Glyph stamps pack holds your glyphs from the Design Kit the same way.

b.x: Because every stroke keeps its pen path, you can change how it was drawn after the fact. Draw, then move a slider, and the stroke is drawn again.

x: Just the last stroke
Changes only the stroke you have just drawn.
Every stroke on this layer
Changes all the strokes on this layer at once.
A slider left alone keeps each stroke as drawn
A slider you do not touch changes nothing, so every stroke keeps its own look.
Back to as drawn
Undoes the adjustment and returns the strokes to exactly how you drew them.

b.x: How to

x: Tap the sliders button in the sidebar.
Last stroke changes the stroke you just made: its size, width swell, clearance, companion, lines.

Whole layer changes every stroke on the layer at once, the way the sliders of your curve library moved every curve. A slider you leave alone keeps each stroke as it was drawn. Double-click a slider to let go of it.
Keep for this brush makes the new settings the brush’s own. Back to as drawn undoes the restyle.

b.x: Whole layer works on a layer made of strokes. A layer with a fill, a paste, a transform or a smudge says so and stays as it is.
Tap the circle in the top strip. Two colours are always ready, the main and the second; X swaps them.

x: Four ways to pick
Disc, Classic, Harmony and Value: four views of the same colours. Use whichever suits.
The disc
Drag round the ring for the colour family and across the middle for how light or deep it is.
What your own writing says this colour means
One line under the disc: what your own writing says the colour means (gold is declaration, for example).
The house palettes
Ready-made palettes: the house colours, the archive’s, and random ones. Tap a colour to use it.

b.x: How to

x: Pick on the disc, or type a hex.
The last ten colours you used are under History.

Palette starts with House: every colour of yours in one place (the brand colours, your house palettes and the site’s colours). Next come two Random palettes, new each time you open the app. Then every palette in the Design Kit: your house palettes as they are, and the rest (your archive, the families of your works, the colour-theory mixes) with near-identical ones merged into one average palette; the number in brackets says how many it stands for.

Under the disc, one line tells you what your own writing says the colour means: gold is declaration, purple spiritual awakening, green stability and growth, oxblood the energy of the personality, and so on. A colour you have not written about says so.
Hold the circle still for a moment and the previous colour comes back.

b.x: Three sliders: hue, saturation, brightness.

x: Hue
Which colour it is: red, yellow, green, blue and round again.
Saturation
How strong the colour is, from grey to full.
Brightness
How light or dark the colour is.
Or type it
Type a colour code, such as #c9a84c.

b.x: Pick a scheme and the colours that go with the one you have are laid out: complementary, split complementary, triad, analogous or tetrad. Tap one to use it.

x: Scheme
Choose a harmony to build from your colour: complementary, analogous, triad and others.
Tap one to use it
Each swatch is one colour of the scheme. Tap it to paint with it.

b.x: The colour you have, from dark to light in ten steps. Good for shading and for checking that a picture works in black and white.

x: The same colour from dark to light
A strip of your colour from dark to light. Tap a step to use it.

b.x: A brush that paints in more than one colour (a companion line, a filled channel, a second channel) shows a swatch for each of its colours at the top of the Colour card and of the brush list.

x: A swatch for each colour of the brush
Every colour the brush uses has its own swatch. Tap one to change that colour.
Colourways: every colour at once
Switches all of the brush’s colours at once to a palette’s colours.

b.x: How to

x: Tap a swatch: Main, Companion (or Second), Channel, Outer channel.
Now the disc, the sliders, Harmony, Value, the hex box and the palettes all change that colour of the brush. Close the card and you are back on the main colour.
Under the swatches, Colourways are your house palettes laid out as sets of colours. One tap recolours every part of the brush at once.
The brush keeps its new colours. Studio, Reset puts the made ones back.

b.x: A brush with one colour shows no swatches: the colour card works as always.
Fill a closed shape by dragging the colour onto it.
How to

x: Drag the colour circle from the top strip onto the canvas and let go.
To set how far “the same colour” reaches, keep holding, then slide sideways before you let go.
On a layer with a Reference layer set, the fill stops at that layer’s lines.

b.x: A plain tap on the circle opens the colour card.
Each new stroke takes the next colour of a palette, in order, the way a screen print goes red, then cyan, then amber.
How to

x: In Actions, choose a palette under Passes.
Draw. The colour steps on after every stroke, and the circle shows the next one.
In the timelapse section, switch on Replay and export by colour pass and the picture is built one colour at a time, in the order the colours first appeared, so the replay shows how it was made.

b.x: Tap the layers button. Each row has a picture, a name, a letter for its blend mode, and an eye. Tap a row to draw on it. Double-click to rename.

x: Layers and groups
The layers, top to bottom. Tap one to draw on it, drag to reorder, and group layers into a folder.
Opacity
How see-through this whole layer is. It changes the layer, not the brush.
Blend mode
How this layer mixes with the ones below it: Multiply, Screen, Overlay and many more.
Glow
Makes the layer give off light, so it can light what is under it.
New layer
Adds a blank layer above the one you are on.
Mask
Adds a mask: paint white to show and black to hide, without erasing anything.
Clip
Clips this layer to the one below, so it only shows where that layer has ink.
Merge
Joins this layer into the one below it.
Group
Puts the layer in a group, a folder with its own eye, name, opacity and blend.
Reference
Marks this layer as the one whose lines ColorDrop and Echo Fill stop at.
Assist
Turns assisted drawing on for this layer only; the row says so.
Make a brush
Turns the marks on this layer into a stamp brush in your Mine pack.
Ghost copy
Puts a faint copy of the layer behind it, as a guide.

b.x: How to

x: Opacity and the Blend mode list apply to the selected layer (or the selected group).
Twenty-six blend modes, the same names Photoshop uses; the letter on the row says which.
Alpha lock keeps painting inside what is already there.
Hold the eye of a layer to see only that layer; hold it again to bring everything back.
Mask: paint white to show, black to hide. Clip clips a layer to the one below. Merge, Duplicate, Clear.
Group puts a layer in a group, which has its own eye, name, opacity and blend mode; collapse it, move it, merge it into one layer, or ungroup. Layers added next to a group member join the group.
Reference marks the layer whose lines ColorDrop and Echo Fill stop at.
Glow makes a layer give off light (see Lights off).
Ghost copy puts a faint copy of the layer behind it.
Assist turns assisted drawing on for this layer only (the row says so).
Make a brush turns the marks on the layer into a stamp.

b.x: Two fingers tapped on a row open its opacity; two fingers swiped across it lock its alpha; two fingers pinched across two rows merge them.

Normal, Multiply, Darken, Color Burn, Linear Burn, Darker Color, Lighten, Screen, Color Dodge, Add, Lighter Color, Overlay, Soft Light, Hard Light, Vivid Light, Linear Light, Pin Light, Hard Mix, Difference, Exclusion, Subtract, Divide, Hue, Saturation, Color, Luminosity.

Seventeen are done by the canvas itself. The other nine are worked out pixel by pixel, so the first time you change a picture with one of them on a very large canvas it takes a moment, and then it is kept.
Copy, Cut and Paste work on the selection, or on the whole layer if nothing is selected.
How to

x: Ctrl C, Ctrl X, Ctrl V, or the buttons in Actions.
Paste puts the picture on a new layer, ready to move: it opens Transform, so move or scale it and tap Done.
A picture copied from another app can be pasted in the same way.

b.x: Choose what the next thing you do affects. Outside the selection the canvas shows diagonal stripes, and painting, erasing, smudging and clearing all stay inside it.

x: Automatic
Selects the area of similar colour where you tap.
Freehand
Draw round what you want to select.
Rectangle
Drag out a box to select.
Add
The next selection is added to the one you have.
Remove
The next selection is taken away from the one you have.
Invert
Swaps what is selected with what is not.
Feather
Softens the edge of the selection.
Copy & Paste
Copies the selected part, or pastes it back as a new layer.
Clear
Deselects everything.

b.x: How to

x: Tap the selection button (or press S) and choose a way: Automatic (tap, and the area of one colour is selected; hold and slide to set how far it reaches), Freehand, Rectangle or Ellipse.
Add and Remove stay on until you tap them again, so you can build a shape in pieces.
Invert swaps inside and outside. Feather softens the edge (0, 8, 20 or 40).
Copy & Paste makes a new layer from the selected part. Clear clears it.
Hold the selection button and the last selection comes back.

b.x: Every selection change is an undo step.
Move, scale, rotate and flip the layer, or just the selected part of it. The blue corners scale, the square edge nodes stretch one way, the green node rotates, and dragging anywhere else moves.

x: Freeform
Stretches each side on its own.
Uniform
Keeps the proportions when you scale.
Distort
Moves each corner independently, to put the picture in perspective.
Warp
Bends the picture with a grid of nodes.
Resampling
How pixels are blended when the picture is stretched: Bicubic (smoothest), Bilinear, or Nearest (hard pixels).
Magnetics
Snaps rotation to 15 degree steps and the centre to the middle of the canvas.
Flip
Mirrors the picture left to right (H) or top to bottom (V).
Fit to canvas
Scales the picture up or down to fit the canvas.
Done
Commits the transform as one step you can undo (Enter does the same; Escape cancels).

b.x: How to

x: Press V, or tap Transform. The pixels lift and the box appears.
Freeform stretches each way; Uniform keeps the shape. Hold Shift while rotating to snap to 15 degrees.
Arrow keys nudge one pixel (Shift for ten). Tapping outside the box nudges it one pixel toward the tap.

The yellow square on the stem below the box sets the point the picture turns round. Drag it anywhere and a yellow ring marks it: the artwork does not move, but rotating (the green node, or Rotate 45) now swings round that ring instead of the middle. Tap the yellow square to put the pivot back at the centre.
Magnetics (off to start) locks rotation to 15 degree steps and the centre to the middle of the canvas.
Resampling chooses Bicubic, Bilinear or Nearest.
Flip, Rotate 45, Fit to canvas, Reset. Done or Enter commits, as one Undo step. Escape cancels.

b.x: If a selection was active it moves with the picture.
Distort moves each corner on its own, with true perspective. Warp gives you a 4 by 4 grid of nodes with a smooth surface through every one.

x: Warp: a grid of nodes
Drag any node and the picture bends smoothly round it.

b.x: How to

x: In Transform, tap Distort or Warp.
Drag a corner (Distort), or a node (Warp). In Warp you can also drag the picture between the nodes and the nearby nodes follow softly.
Tap Freeform or Uniform to go back to the original shape.

b.x: Flip, Rotate 45 and Fit work before you Distort or Warp, not after.
Guides are lines the stroke can lock to: a grid, isometric lines, or perspective with one, two or three vanishing points. Assisted drawing makes the stroke follow them.
How to

x: In Actions, choose a Guide. Pick a grid size for the grid.
For perspective, drag the coloured points to move the vanishing points. They can sit far outside the canvas: zoom out to reach them. Switch Move vanishing points off to draw near them.
Turn on Assisted drawing, in Actions or for one layer with the Assist button in the Layers card. A stroke locks to the nearest guide direction once it has moved a little.

b.x: In perspective, strokes lock to the lines toward each vanishing point, and to the vertical in one- and two-point guides.
The stroke repeats across a guide as you draw it: vertical, horizontal, quadrant, or radial with eight parts.
Draw a shape roughly, then hold the pen still at the end. It snaps to a straight line, a triangle, a four-sided shape or an ellipse.
How to

x: Draw, then hold still for about half a second.
While it is held, touch a second finger to the screen (or press Shift) and it becomes perfect: a line at the nearest 15 degrees, a circle, a square, an equilateral triangle.

b.x: You can switch QuickShape off in Actions.
In your canvas plate the long curve is never drawn: it is many short marks whose ends line up across a gap. Tangent Lock helps you do that.
How to

x: Turn on Tangent Lock in Actions.
Start a stroke just beyond the end of an earlier one, roughly in line with it.
The start slides onto that line, a gold ring shows where it caught, and the correction fades over the first few widths so the rest of the stroke is yours.

b.x: Turn a stroke into straight segments with rounded corners, or go from smooth to faceted partway along, the hard change of your faceted-and-curved plates.
How to

x: Choose All strokes faceted in Actions, or
hold Shift while you draw: the stroke is as you drew it until the moment you press Shift, and facets after.

b.x: Draw a base, press one button, and fill in the middle. The picture repeats with no visible seam: for all-over prints, cuffs and belts.

b.alt: Make the tile, fill the middle, check the repeat
x: Nine copies side by side
The picture repeated three by three, so a seam would show.
What to look for
A seam shows as a break where one copy ends and the next begins. If you see one, slide the picture half way round again and fill it.
Done
Closes the repeat sheet.

b.x: How to

x: Draw the base. Keep your marks away from the edges of the canvas: anything that touches an edge is cut there and will leave a seam. Leave the corners open, because that is where you will be drawing next. Several of the same motif looks more random than one of each.

In Actions, under Drawing Assist, tap Make tile: slide the picture half way round. Everything on every layer slides half way across and half way down and wraps, so the old edges are now the middle. Wrapping turns on by itself.
Fill in the middle. Draw into the empty cross where the edges met. A mark that runs off one side comes back on the opposite side, so nothing you add can spoil the seam. Do not leave the wrapping off.

A medallion in the middle? Tap Add the corner copies. A copy of the layer slides half way round, so the four corners hold quarter copies of the middle and the whole thing repeats round it. Draw into the gaps that are left.
Tap Check the repeat (3 by 3) to see nine copies side by side. If you can see where one copy ends and the next begins, slide it half way round again and fill that seam.
It is one step you can undo. Sliding twice puts the picture exactly where it started. The slide and the check are also in the QuickMenu and in Gesture Controls.

b.x: Tile on Horizontal wraps sideways only (for a cuff or a belt); Both ways wraps in both directions.
Use the Seamless tile canvas size for square repeats.
Show the tiles around draws the neighbours faintly beside the canvas while you work.
When Tile is on, the canvas shows you where a line comes out on the other side, and where an end is still missing its partner.
How to

x: The ghost. As your pen heads for an edge, a dashed line and a ring appear on the exact opposite side, at the place the line will come back in and along the way it is heading. Aim for the ring and the line runs on without a break.
Starting near an edge. The ghost also shows where a line arriving from the other side would have to end, so you can meet it.
The gate. Wherever your art touches one edge and nothing meets it on the opposite edge, a gate marks the place to connect, with a dot where the art is. Draw the matching end and the gate goes away.
The dotted cross. A faint dotted cross through the middle shows where the old edges lie after Make tile: that is where the seams are.
Switch them off with Smart guides under Drawing Assist if you want a clean canvas.

b.x: The guides only show when Tile is Horizontal or Both ways. With Horizontal, only left and right are watched.
The guides are never part of your picture: they are not drawn into the layers, the export or the timelapse.

secs.title: Seam mode: draw on a garment

b.x: A garment laid flat, every piece Printful sews, on one canvas. A line that runs off a sewn edge carries on, as you draw, on the piece that edge is sewn to, so it is unbroken on the finished garment.
How to

x: Start one. Actions > New canvas > Hoodie 717 zip (seams). The pieces appear with Printful’s own cut lines, safe areas and fold lines under your drawing; they are a guide and are never saved into the art.
The numbers. Each sewn edge is drawn in a colour with a number. The same number and colour appear on the edge it is sewn to: 19 on the front sews to 19 on the back.

Draw across. Run a stroke off a coloured edge and it continues on its partner, at the same place along the seam and turned to that edge, never mirrored. Keep drawing past the edge and it keeps going, through the next seam and the next, round the garment, until it leaves at a hem, a cuff or the hood’s face. It is never drawn on the piece that happens to sit beside it on the sheet.
The zip. The two front halves are sewn at the zipper (21), so a line across the chest runs straight on.
Turn it off. Actions > Seam mode (toggle) stops the carrying; the coloured edges fade.

Print files. Actions > Save print files (garment) writes the seven files Printful takes at 5250 x 6000: front, back, hood, both sleeves, the pocket (cut from the front where it is sewn) and the inside.

Good to know. The waistband and cuffs fold in half; only their outer half is carried to. A line that leaves exactly at a corner where three pieces meet stops there; one stroke travels through up to six pieces.

b.x: An outline the size of your brush follows the mouse or the hovering pen, so you see where a mark will land and how big it will be.

x: The ring: the size of the brush
An outline at the brush’s size that follows the mouse or the hovering pen. It is never drawn into the picture.

b.x: How to

x: Move the mouse or hover the pen over the canvas. A thin ring appears at the size of the brush, at the zoom you are working at.
It changes with the size slider, with zoom, and with the tool: Paint, Smudge and Erase each show their own size.
A finger has no hover, so the ring does not show on touch.
To switch it off, untick Brush cursor under Drawing Assist in Actions. It stays off until you tick it again.

b.x: The ring is a guide only: it is never drawn into the picture.
Fill a closed shape with concentric lines that follow its edge inward, collapsing to its middle: the fill of your spec, the thing that makes a piece read dense instead of sparse.

x: Space, line, first gap, number of echoes
Echo Fill: how far apart the lines are, how thick they are, the gap before the first, and how many there are.

b.x: How to

x: In Actions, tap Echo Fill. The bar appears.
Set Space (distance between lines), Line (thickness), First gap (distance from the edge to the first line) and Echoes (how many).
Tap inside a closed shape. It fills with your current colour.
Tap Done when finished.

b.x: Set a Reference layer first and the shape is found from its lines, not the layer you draw on.
Draw a line and it gets yellow nodes. Drag a node and the line bends through its new place, drawn again with the same brush.

x: Done removes the nodes; Keep editing leaves them
Done ends Node mode and takes the handles away; Keep editing hides the bar but leaves the nodes there to move again.

b.x: How to

x: In Actions, open Assist and tap Node mode.
Draw a line. Yellow nodes appear along it; the first and last are its ends.
Press a node and drag. The line bends between its two neighbours and stays put beyond them. Let go and the stroke is drawn again through the new path.

The nodes stay put until you say so. Press anywhere that is not a node and a bar asks Finish this line?: Done removes the nodes so the next press draws a new line, Keep editing leaves them. Tap Node mode again to turn it off.

b.x: How many nodes (Few, Some, Many) sits under the button: fewer nodes bend the line in broad curves, more give you finer control.
One Undo takes the whole line away, however many times you moved it.

Any line on the layer: with Node mode on and no nodes showing, press on a line you drew earlier and it gets its nodes. Drag one and only that line bends; the layer is redrawn in the same order, so nothing else moves. One Undo puts it back. To draw a new line, start on bare canvas.
Only strokes made with a brush have nodes (not a fill, a pasted part or a smudge). If the layer has fills, pasted or smudged parts, only the last line you drew can be bent.
Interlace: the Weave hero goes over at the first crossing, under at the next, over at the next, with a clean gap at each. About one piece in six in your archive is interlaced.

secs.title: Glow, Lights off and the lit cell

b.x: Like your glow painting: dark lines on a luminous ground.
How to

x: In the Layers card, move Glow up on a layer. It gives off a soft light.
In Actions, Lights off darkens everything that does not glow, so only the glowing layers show. Press it again for the lights.
Light one makes one region the lit cell: tap inside a closed shape and it becomes its own glowing layer, called Lit cell, and nothing else changes.

b.x: Lights off is how you see it. A saved PNG is always with the lights on.
The wand button. Eleven effects, live on the layer, inside the selection if there is one.

x: Choose an effect
Pick what to apply: Hue, Saturation, Blur, Curves, Noise and more.
Its settings, live
Sliders for the effect. The picture changes as you move them.
Apply
Keeps the effect, as one step you can undo.
Cancel
Throws the effect away and leaves the layer as it was.

b.x: How to

x: Choose an effect. Move its settings and the layer changes as you do.
Apply keeps it (one Undo step). Cancel puts it back.
Hue, saturation, brightness
Colour balance
Curves
Gradient map
Uses your house palettes
Gaussian blur
Motion blur
Noise
Sharpen
Bloom
Halftone
Chromatic aberration

chapters.title: Recording, studying and showing your hand

b.x: PL Paint records a timelapse of every picture as you draw. Replay it, scrub it, or turn it into a video.

x: Scrub
Drag along the bar to jump to any moment of the drawing.
Pause
Stops or restarts the replay.
Close
Closes the replay and takes you back to the canvas.

b.x: How to

x: In Actions, find the Timelapse section. Replay plays it; drag the slider to scrub.
Export 30-second video or Export full video saves a webm.
Replay and export by colour pass shows the picture built one colour at a time.

Export alive makes a video that is built by accumulation for four seconds, then breathes for six: every part of the finished picture drifts slowly on its own cycle, looping with no seam. It never freezes.

b.x: The Recording switch turns the timelapse off for a picture.

The timelapse keeps the picture. Study keeps your hand: the real path of the pen with pressure and tilt, how the pen approaches before it touches, your pauses, your undos, how you zoom and rotate, and a small picture every tenth stroke. It is how Third Eye learns to draw like you.

x: Name the session
Gives this recording a name, so you can find it later.
New canvas
Starts a blank picture to record on.
The guided exercises
Short drawing exercises (lines, curves, circles) that teach the app your hand.
Start
Begins recording.

b.x: How to

x: In Actions, tap Study: record how I draw.
Name the session. Leave New canvas on: the study draws on its own canvas, named “hand study”, so the hand model finds it.
Tap Start the study. A red dot appears at the top, and a bar tells you the exercise.
Do the exercises in order, or pick one from the card. The bar counts your strokes and moves on by itself.
Tap Mark at any moment and say in a few words what you are doing, so the record knows.
Tap Stop when you are finished.

b.x: The twelve exercises: curves end to end, slow then fast, crossings, starts and ends, light to heavy, as steady as you can, doubles, filling a shape, your mark, your glyphs, fixing a mistake, and a free page. Each one says what it teaches.
The files stay in Documents, in PL Paint. Nothing is sent anywhere.
The dot at the top right shows the minutes and the number of strokes. The bar under the top strip shows the exercise.

x: Recording
Shows that the study is recording your hand.
The exercise, how many done, Mark, Next, Stop
The exercise you are on, how many you have done, Mark to keep a good one, Next, and Stop.

b.x: A one-page record of how a piece was drawn, made from its own stroke log: how many strokes, how long the pen was on the glass, the length of line, the median speed, the pressure, the shake, which brushes, and a fingerprint of the record.
How to

x: In Actions, tap Hand Trace. A PNG page and a small file are saved.

b.x: It is a record of process. It shows the hand at work. It does not prove who drew the piece and it is not a signature.
Take a photo of a physical drawing and lift the ink off the paper onto a transparent layer, the edge kept as you drew it.

x: The ink, lifted
The drawing with the paper taken out, as it will become a layer.
Threshold
Where the line falls between ink and paper. Lower lifts more; higher lifts only the darkest.
Dust
Throws away the tiny specks the paper leaves.
Light ink on dark paper
Switch on when your marks are lighter than the ground.
Lift the ink
Makes the layer from the lifted ink.

b.x: How to

x: In Actions, tap Lift and choose a photo.
Threshold says how dark counts as ink. Softness is how gradual the edge is. Gain is how strongly. Remove specks throws away dust.
Tick Light ink on dark paper for chalk or glow on black.
Leave Keep the ink’s own colours on, or turn it off and the ink takes your current colour.
Tap Lift the ink. It arrives on its own layer.

b.x: The paper is found area by area, so a shadow across the photo is not mistaken for ink.

One tap offers a name for the work. If you put a file called names-bank.txt in the PL Paint folder (one name per line, or Name - QUALITY), the names come from it, one after another. Without one, it offers one of the qualities you write about, such as elegance, mystery, resilience, with the date.

chapters.title: On your phone, and in step

secs.title: Put PL Paint on your iPhone

b.x: The iPhone version is the same app, installed from Safari. It opens full screen with no browser around it, and it works with no signal once it has opened once.
How to

x: On the iPhone, open Safari and go to the PL Paint address (it ends in /paint/).
Tap the Share button, then Add to Home Screen, then Add.
Open PL Paint from the Home Screen, not from Safari. The installed app keeps its own storage, so everything below is done inside it.
Open Actions, then Sync, paste your sync key, and tap Connect. Your works arrive.

b.x: An iPhone clears the saved data of a web page it has not seen for about a week. Sync is what makes that safe: your works are also kept in your private store, so open the app and they come back.
To update the app, close it and open it again with a signal. It picks up the newest version by itself.

On a phone the picture fills the screen. The tools fold into one button at the top left: the tool in your hand and three dots. Tap the dots and the toolbar opens into two rows: Paint, Smudge, Erase, Layers and Colour on top; Gallery (the arrow), Actions, Adjustments, Selection and Transform below. Tap the dots again to fold it. The sliders sit small on the right. Cards open from the bottom as sheets, and Actions is in tabs: Canvas, Assist, Hand, Video, Prefs.

x: The tool in your hand
The tool you are using now, with its size.
The dots: open the toolbar
Opens the toolbar that is folded away to give the canvas room.
Size
The slider on the left. Makes the brush bigger or smaller.
Opacity
The second slider. How see-through the brush is.
Undo
Takes back the last thing you did.

b.x: How to

x: A finger draws, because a phone has no pen, and a finger does everything the pen does: select, transform, pick a colour with Modify, place a vanishing point, Echo Fill. Two fingers move, zoom and turn the canvas, and a two-finger tap undoes.

A phone has less memory for pictures than a laptop, so it holds a number of layers that depends on the canvas size (about seven at 2048 x 1536). When you reach it, it says so: merge some layers, or start smaller.
A phone cannot tell a light touch from a hard one, so pressure stays the same. Use Speed to size in the Brush Studio (Dynamics) when you want the line to thin and thicken.
Save PNG, Save PSD, Save SVG and the video exports open the iPhone Share sheet: Save to Photos, Save to Files, send in Messages.
Landscape works too. Turn the phone and the app fits itself to the screen.
The first canvas on a phone is the phone’s own screen, upright.

b.x: A very large canvas takes memory. If the phone struggles, work at 2048 on the long side and Sync it to the laptop for the final.
Top row: the tools for marks. Bottom row: the tools for the whole picture. The arrow at the start of the bottom row is the Gallery.

x: Paint
The brush. Draws with the brush you have chosen.
Smudge
The finger. Pushes the colour that is already there, instead of adding new colour.
Erase
The eraser. Takes ink away. It remembers its own brush and size.
Layers
The stack of sheets your picture is made of.
Colour
The coloured circle. A tap opens the colour card; the circle always shows the colour you are painting with.
Fold
Folds the toolbar away to give the canvas room.
Gallery
The list of everything you have drawn. Open a work, start a new one, or look at your Daily Mark.
Actions
The wrench. Files, the video of your drawing, guides, drawing assists and the settings.
Adjustments
The wand. Colour and picture effects such as Hue, Blur and Curves, applied to the layer you are on.
Selection
The S shape. Marks off part of the picture, so only that part changes.
Transform
The arrow. Lifts the layer so you can move, scale, rotate or bend it.

b.x: Actions, Layers, Colour, Brushes, Adjustments and Adjust strokes open as sheets from the bottom of the screen. Tap the same button again, or tap the canvas, to close the sheet.

x: Cards open from the bottom as sheets, clear of the sliders
On the phone, settings open as sheets from the bottom, so they never cover the sliders.

secs.title: Settings: make the app look the way you like

b.x: Actions, then Settings. Every change shows at once and is kept on this device.

x: Glass blur
How soft the glass is: higher blurs what sits behind the panels more.
How much shows through the glass
The see-through amount: higher lets more of the canvas show through the panels.
The curve tile behind everything
The house curve tile drawn under the glass, as a quiet pattern; turn it off for a plain ground.
Text size
The size of all reading text in the app, from small to large.
Font for reading text
Which house font the app reads in; the brushes and your drawing are not changed by it.
Back to the house look
Puts every setting on this panel back to how PL Paint ships.

b.x: How to

x: The glass. Blur sets how soft the glass panels are; see-through sets how much of the picture and the tile shows through them.
The tile. Your curve tile sits behind the app. Slide it up to see it more, down to zero to hide it.
Text. Text size makes the menus larger or smaller. Font picks the face for reading text: your hand, Jost, Cormorant or Courier Prime. Headlines keep their own faces.
Reduce motion. Turns off the animations.
Back to the house look. Puts every setting back.
PL Paint stays dark: the colours in your picture read truest against it.

secs.title: Sync: the same works on every device

b.x: Draw on the laptop, open the phone, and the work is there. Draw on the phone, open the laptop, and it is there too.

x: Where it stands
Says whether this device is connected and when it last synced.
What this device is called
A name for this device, so you can tell your devices apart.
Paste the key here, once
Paste your sync key. It is never shown again after you connect.
Connect
Joins this device to your others.
Done
Closes this card. Syncing carries on.

b.x: How to

x: The key. One key joins your devices. The laptop picks it up from a file called sync-key.txt in the PL Paint folder (Documents, PL Paint), connects, and removes the file. On the phone, paste it once into Actions, Sync, then tap Connect.
When it syncs. When the app opens, about twenty seconds after you stop drawing, when you leave the app, and when you tap Sync now.

What goes across. Your works (the picture, its name, its stack), the days in your Daily Mark, and the brushes in Mine. When you change a Mine brush on one device, the newer change wins on the other the next time they sync. A blank first page is not sent.
What stays. Study sessions never leave the computer they were made on. The key is never shown again after you connect.
If both devices changed the same work. Nothing is overwritten. The other copy arrives as a second work named “(other device)”, and you keep the one you like.
Deleting. Delete a work on one device and it is deleted on the others the next time they sync.
Forget the key disconnects a device. Its works stay on it.

b.x: Where it stands is written at the top of the Sync card: up to date, syncing, offline (it tries again by itself), or the key was refused.
Brushes in Mine are added on every device; changing one that already exists on both is not carried across. Duplicate it under a new name to share the new version.

secs.title: Send a finished piece to Curate or the Archive

b.x: When a piece is done, send it on from the app. It leaves from the laptop or the phone the same way.

x: What it will do
Says what Send will do, and whether Sync is connected.
The title it is filed under
The name the piece is filed under. It starts as the work’s name.
To Curate
Sends the picture to the Curate deck.
To the Archive
Sends the picture to the archive as a digital work, which gets the next PL number.
Done
Closes this card.

b.x: How to

x: Open Actions, then Send to Curate or the Archive. The card needs Sync connected, because the same key sends your pieces.
Check the Title (it starts as the work’s name), then tap To Curate or To the Archive. The whole picture goes as a PNG. If the background is hidden, it stays transparent.
To Curate: the piece waits in a private outbox. The next time a session opens (or when you say file the sends ) it is filed into Curate and shows after the gallery deploys.
To the Archive: the same wait, then the next free PL number is stamped on it as a digital piece. Nothing is published to the public archive until you say so.

b.x: If the Archive finds a near copy of a piece it already holds, it stops without using a number and the piece stays in the outbox until you rule it a separate work.
Sending does not remove or change your work.
Everything is in the Documents folder, in PL Paint.

Your works and the gallery index
study-....json
Study sessions (events, one file per few seconds, and an index)
daily.json
The days you drew (Daily Mark)

Your own list of names, if you make one

The brush list, the QuickMenu and Gesture controls
Kept inside the app, and exported with Export this pack
